title: Opaque Metadata Gateway & Span Correlation Proxy
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: We see inconsistent span correlation across mixed-transport requests (HTTP -> websocket -> async worker queues) and brittle header parsing that causes sampling/trace losses for legacy clients. This ticket implements an Opaque Metadata Gateway (OMG) — a thin proxying layer and SDK hook that normalizes incoming request metadata into a compact, transport-agnostic carrier and emits a stable span correlation token for downstream services and async workers. The goal is to reduce trace gaps, preserve sampling decisions, and avoid breaking older clients that rely on nonstandard headers.
background_and_goals:
- Support cross-transport propagation (HTTP/gRPC/WebSocket/worker-queues) with a single canonical carrier used inside our edge and SDKs.
- Preserve sampling decision and original trace identifiers when available; otherwise emit a trace-safe correlation token tied to request lifecycle.
- Provide a proxyable gateway component that can be deployed at the edge and in sidecar form for Dedicated/Private deployments.
- Minimize per-request overhead (target < 150us added P50 at edge path) and a small memory footprint for high-throughput paths.
design_decisions_and_tradeoffs:
- Use a compact binary carrier encoded as base64 when crossing binary transports to avoid header size problems; HTTP path will use a short header prefix 'x-rw-meta'.
- Keep compatibility layer that will parse legacy headers (b3, traceparent, custom-legacy) in a permissive first-responder strategy; prefer explicit canonical carrier if present.
- Avoid changing sampling algorithm: propagate sampling bit rather than re-evaluating at the gateway. This keeps traces comparable across environments but requires coordinating with sampling config ops.
- Chose proxy approach over rewriting app SDKs first to get rollout speed; long-term plan is to add direct SDK hook to obviate proxy for some languages.
implementation_plan:
1) Edge proxy component that normalizes incoming headers into OMG carrier and attaches correlation-token header. 2) SDK hook (Node + Go initial) to read OMG carrier from request context, map to OpenTelemetry/OTLP context, and forward token on outgoing calls. 3) Worker queue extension to attach carrier as envelope metadata on messages (SQS/Kafka). 4) Backfill compatibility parser for b3/traceparent/custom. 5) Canary & rollout via feature-flagged routing in edge.
Milestones:
- PoC edge proxy + Node SDK hook (2w)
- Integration tests + perf harness (1w)
- Go SDK hook + queue support (1w)
- Canary in prod + dashboarding (1w)
acceptance_criteria: Edge proxy accepts legacy headers (b3, traceparent, xx-custom) and emits x-rw-meta when normalized
Node and Go SDK hooks read x-rw-meta and reconstruct OpenTelemetry context reliably in >= 99% of sampled flows
Trace gaps (broken parent-child linking) reduce by >= 70% for the measured 7-day test traffic between edge and async workers
Performance: added P50 latency on edge path under 95th percentile load < 150 microseconds; P99 spike < 2ms
Feature-gated canary deploy with automatic rollback on increased trace error rate or latency regressions
dashboard_and_alerts: Create 'OMG Propagation' dashboard in Console with distribution of carrier sizes, normalize latency, cross-transport parent loss rate, and canary health. Alert if traces.gap_rate_cross_transport increases by > 25% vs baseline or omg.normalize.success_rate < 98% for 10m.
rollout_plan: 1) Deploy proxy & Node SDK in staging, run synthetic traffic for 48h. 2) Canary 5% in prod (low-traffic region) for 2h, monitor dashboards. 3) Expand to 25% for 6h if stable, then 100% over 24h. 4) Deploy Go SDK and queue integrations in parallel with canary expansion. 5) Deprecate legacy header-only path after 6 weeks with telemetry to track remaining legacy clients.
data_privacy_considerations: Carrier must not include PII; strip any header fields matching known sensitive keys. When customers deploy Private, the OMG component runs in their VPC and logs must not leave customer network. Documented in privacy runbook.
related_work_notes: Coordination required with runtime-1.18 kernel-selection team for low-latency path in edge binary
Follow-on ticket planned to add Java/Python SDK hooks after initial Node/Go rollout
Discussed with Security (Sasha Liu) — need KMS key access for canary telemetry masking
